title: C Programming Language Question Bank
subject: C Programming
description: Comprehensive 20-question bank covering C fundamentals, pointers, memory, data structures, and functions.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: What is the guaranteed minimum size of a `char` data type in C standard?
questions.explanation: In standard C, sizeof(char) is defined to be exactly 1 byte.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to immediately terminate a `for` or `while` loop in C?
questions.explanation: `break` terminates execution of the nearest enclosing loop or switch statement.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: What happens when you attempt to dereference a wild or uninitialized pointer in C?
options: It causes undefined behavior or segmentation fault
The compiler throws a syntax error
correctAnswers: It causes undefined behavior or segmentation fault
questions.explanation: Dereferencing uninitialized pointers accesses arbitrary memory, leading to undefined behavior or crash.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Given the snippet below, what is the value of `x` after execution?
questions.explanation: `*p = 25` modifies the value at memory address `&x`, changing `x` to 25.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Which standard header file must be included to use `malloc()`, `calloc()`, and `free()`?
questions.explanation: `<stdlib.h>` contains prototypes for dynamic memory allocation functions in C.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: What is the key difference between `char str1[] = "hello";` and `char *str2 = "hello";`?
options: str1 is stored in read-only memory, while str2 is on the stack
str1 is a modifiable array on the stack; str2 points to a read-only string literal
str1 requires free(), while str2 does not
correctAnswers: str1 is a modifiable array on the stack; str2 points to a read-only string literal
questions.explanation: Modifying elements of str1 is valid; modifying characters via str2 causes undefined behavior.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Which of the following are valid integer constant representations in C?
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal (0x), Octal (0 prefix), and Long suffix (L) are standard ANSI C constants.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Which of the following functions are used for dynamic memory management in C?
questions.explanation: `malloc`, `calloc`, and `realloc` manage heap allocation in standard C.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Which statements correctly describe a `union` in C?
options: All members share the same starting memory location
Total memory allocated is equal to the size of its largest member
Writing a new member overwrites the value of previously written members
Every member has its own separate memory address
correctAnswers: All members share the same starting memory location
Total memory allocated is equal to the size of its largest member
Writing a new member overwrites the value of previously written members
questions.explanation: A union allows storing different data types in the same shared memory space.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Which of the following keywords perform explicit control flow jumps in C?
questions.explanation: All 4 keywords transfer control to another instruction address.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: In C, array indexing is 0-based, meaning the first element of `int arr[5]` is `arr[0]`.
questions.explanation: C arrays always start at index 0 up to size - 1.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Standard C supports native function overloading (defining multiple functions with identical names but different parameter signatures).
questions.explanation: Standard C does not support function overloading; C++ introduced function overloading.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: The `malloc()` function automatically initializes all allocated bytes to zero.
questions.explanation: `malloc()` leaves memory uninitialized (garbage values); `calloc()` initializes memory to zero.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: A structure definition in C can contain a pointer member pointing to a structure of the same type.
questions.explanation: Self-referential structures (e.g. `struct Node { int data; struct Node *next; };`) form linked lists and trees.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: What keyword is used in C to declare a variable whose value cannot be modified after initialization?
questions.explanation: The `const` type qualifier makes a variable read-only.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: What unary operator symbol is used in C to obtain the memory address of a variable?
questions.explanation: The ampersand `&` is the address-of operator.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: What standard C library function is used to close an open file stream `FILE *fp`?
questions.explanation: `fclose(fp)` flushes buffers and closes the file stream.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Write a recursive C function `int factorial(int n)` that returns the factorial of non-negative integer `n`.
questions.explanation: Base case: n <= 1 returns 1. Recursive case: n * factorial(n - 1).

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Write a C function `void swap(int *a, int *b)` that swaps the integer values pointed to by `a` and `b`.
questions.explanation: Store *a in temp, assign *b to *a, and assign temp to *b.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.questionText: Write a C function `int string_length(const char *str)` that returns the length of a null-terminated string without using `<string.h>`.
questions.explanation: Iterate through pointer array until null terminator '\0' is encountered.
